name: Zapfloor
tagline: Management software for coworking and flex office spaces: memberships, desk and meeting room bookings, credits, invoicing, and door access.

pricing.notes: AI-drafted from a site submission; price unverified.

verdictSummary: The visible core is a resource calendar with membership rules bolted on: who can book what, how many credits they have left, and what that adds up to at the end of the month. An agent can produce that in a weekend and it will genuinely work for one small space with a few dozen members. What it will not produce is the boring half that makes the product sellable: smart lock and access control integrations, accounting exports, VAT-correct invoicing, a member mobile app, and a white-labelled portal you can hand to tenants without embarrassment. If you run one floor and are happy invoicing by hand, build it. If you run several sites with turnstiles and an accountant, do not.
coreLoopDIY: A self-hosted booking app where members log in, see desks and meeting rooms on a calendar, book against a monthly credit allowance, and get a month-end usage summary you can turn into invoices.
requirements: A small server or VPS to host it on
Optional: Stripe keys if you want card payments instead of manual invoicing
Someone to keep the member list current
whatYouLose: Access control integrations: your DIY build will not open the front door or a smart lock
Proper invoicing: tax handling, credit notes, dunning, and accounting exports are all on you
Member mobile apps and a polished branded portal for tenants
Multi-site, multi-currency, multi-team plan logic that scales past one floor
Someone to call when the booking calendar breaks on a Monday morning
moatNotes: The sticky part is not the calendar, it is the wiring into locks, printers, payment providers and accounting software that a space already depends on.
whyPeopleStillPay: Because a coworking operator is not buying a booking grid, they are buying the thing that makes the door open, the invoice go out with the right VAT on it, and the numbers land in their accounting package without a spreadsheet in the middle. That work is unglamorous, integration-heavy, and expensive to maintain per vendor. Operators also have staff who need to use the tool without training, and members who judge the space partly by how bad the booking app is. Paying a few hundred a month to not own any of that is an easy call once you are past one small floor.
notes: Great one-shot if your coworking space is one room with a coffee machine; less great once there is a turnstile.
prompt:
Build a self-hosted coworking space booking and membership app. Single operator, single site.

Stack, no substitutions:
- Next.js (App Router, TypeScript) with Tailwind
- SQLite via Drizzle ORM, file at ./data/app.db
- Auth: email magic links via a single SMTP account, session cookie, no third party auth provider
- Runs with `npm run dev` on localhost and deploys as a plain Node server

Data model:
- Member: name, email, company, plan, monthlyCredits, active flag, role (member | staff)
- Resource: name, type (desk | meeting_room | phone_booth), capacity, hourlyCredits, open hours, color
- Booking: member, resource, start, end, creditsCharged, status (confirmed | cancelled)
- CreditLedger: member, month, creditsIncluded, creditsUsed, overageCredits

Features in scope:
- Member view: week calendar per resource type, click an empty slot to book, see own bookings, cancel with a configurable cutoff (default 2 hours)
- Booking rules enforced server side: no double booking, respect resource open hours, max booking length, refuse if it would exceed remaining monthly credits unless the member plan allows overage
- Staff view: CRUD members and resources, book on behalf of a member, see today's occupancy, override rules with a logged reason
- Month-end report page: per member credits included, used, overage, and a CSV export for invoicing
- Seed script with 3 resources and 5 members so the app is usable on first run

Explicitly out of scope, do not attempt:
- Smart lock or access control integrations
- Payment processing, tax calculation, real invoices
- Mobile apps, multi-site, white labelling, email marketing

Requirements:
- All config in .env: SMTP creds, SESSION_SECRET, SITE_NAME, TIMEZONE. Ship .env.example.
- No telemetry, no external analytics, no CDN fonts.
- Timezone-correct booking math, store timestamps in UTC, render in TIMEZONE.
- Vitest tests for the booking rule engine: overlap, credit limits, cutoff, open hours.
- README with setup, seed, and how to add a resource.
